The architect, Ali bin Muhammad of Sarakhs (now just across the border from Turkmenistan in Iran), was so pleased with his work that he signed the tower in the baked bricks. But assuming that at least some of the architects and builders of these monumental towers were local and possibly Persian (Tajik), who was it who conceived the idea of erecting them, and who paid for their construction? A clever researcher from Kyrgyzstan, D. Imankulov, has recently come up with a highly innovative insight on this issue. Using modern technologies, he measured the height of a number of major minarets of the Karakhanid lands from the eleventh and twelfth centuries.
